title: safety-signal-heuristic-ontology-draft
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working sketch of a compact, adoptable ontology for the safety and fidelity signals we use to gate incremental exposure (canaries / micro-releases / A/B experiments) of LLM-powered features via Console rollouts. Goal is practical: make signal names, semantics, and heuristic wiring small and predictable so engineers + stewards can agree quickly when to pause, quarantine, or roll forward.

Status / context:
- Working draft for cross-functional review (product, SRE, evals, research, monitoring).
- Related artifacts: CONFLUENCE-1234 (signal catalog), JIRA-ROLL-789 (canary infra work), PR 314 (console signal UI).
- This is intentionally prescriptive but small — we should avoid a giant taxonomy that becomes unmaintainable.

Scope / assumptions:
- Focus on runtime safety, behavioral regressions, latency/cost degradations, and user-impact heuristics for staged exposure of LLM features (frontend LLM prompts, rerankers, assistant responses).
- Not covering offline evals or human-label pipelines in depth (those belong in Eval team's docs) — but include quick hooks back to those systems.

Core signal families (high-level):
1) Fidelity Signals — indicate model output quality changes vs baseline:
   - hallucination-rate: fraction of responses flagged by automated checks as containing unsupported facts (heuristics + model-based verifier).
   - prompt-compliance-fail: fraction of responses violating structural constraints (JSON schema, required fields, policy checklist).
   - semantic-drift-score: distributional shift vs baseline embedding centroid (fast, noisy proxy).

2) Safety Signals — user-visible safety problems: toxic-content-rate, PII-extraction-rate, policy-violation-flag-count.

3) Reliability Signals — system-level health: token-latency-p50/p90/p99, error-rate-4xx, error-rate-5xx, kvcache-miss-rate, oom-events.

4) Cost & Efficiency Signals — operational economics: tokens-per-request, avg-gpu-seconds-per-request, batched-throughput.

5) Business Impact Proxies — higher-level metrics that matter to product: conversion-delta (from experiment), retention-proxy, abandon-rate-after-response.

Signal primitives and canonical names (short-list to implement first):
- fidelity.hallucination_rate
- fidelity.schema_violation_rate
- safety.policy_violation_count
- reliability.request_p99_ms
- reliability.server_error_rate
- cost.tokens_per_session
- biz.abandon_after_first_reply_pct

Why these primitives?
- They map cleanly to console dashboards and to automatic gates (e.g., absolute thresholds or relative delta vs baseline).
- Keep names hierarchical for easy filtering and RBAC views.

Mapping to telemetry sources (quick sketch):
- hallucination_rate <- verifier microservice (models: verifier-v2), batch off-path flags + sampling to human-review.
- schema_violation_rate <- response-validator library instrumented in SDK and proxy.
- policy_violation_count <- policy-detector stream (fast model + static rules); high-confidence hits escalate to safety team channel.
- request_p99_ms & server_error_rate <- platform traces + metrics (Prometheus, OpenTelemetry).
- cost metrics <- billing/export pipeline + token counters in runtime.

Heuristics for gating (proposed, to iterate):
- Absolute thresholds: stop exposure if policy_violation_count > 0.5% (user-visible infra), or if server_error_rate > 2% sustained 5m.
- Relative deltas: if fidelity.hallucination_rate increases by >50% vs baseline and absolute >1%, pause.
- Latency SLO breach: if request_p99_ms > 2x baseline AND customer-visible error rate increases, throttle or route to fallback model.
- Multi-signal guard: only trigger auto-quarantine when 2 independent families degrade (e.g., fidelity + reliability), to reduce noise-driven rollbacks.

Signal aggregation windows and sampling guidance:
- Default window: 5m for fast ops signals (latency, error), 1h for behavioral signals (hallucination, policy).
- Sampling: we must surface both sampled human-label rates and fast automated heuristics. Human labels are slow but higher fidelity — include them as an optional second-tier gate.

Experiment activation patterns (examples):
- Microcanary (1%): send 1% of traffic -> monitor 5m operational signals + 1h behavioral. If anything trips, immediate rollback.
- Staged A/B (50/50): only after 24h of stable microcanary + offline evals. Include business proxies in 24–72h watch window.

Runbook snippets (to embed in Console):
- Emergency pause: "scope traffic to baseline model" + notify #oncall-product + create incident (JIRA-INC-xxx).
- Quarantine: "move traffic to quarantine slice (observability-only) and increase sampling rate for human labeling".
- Escalation: "safety lead pager if policy_violation_count persists > threshold for 30m".

Observation & human-in-loop flows:
- When automated heuristics flag an issue, create a lightweight review ticket with: sample responses, signal deltas, recent deploy ID, canary slice id.
- Assign to owner: product + SRE + safety. Owner must triage within 1h for microcanary, 6h for A/B.

Dashboard / Console UX suggestions (short):
- Compact signal panel per rollout: three tiles (Operational, Behavioral, Safety) with delta vs baseline + trend sparkline.
- One-click freeze/route-back button (requires 2 approvals for >5% traffic).
- Telemetry drilldown: sample payloads (sanitized) + confidence scores + causal annotate (deploy id, model variant).

Open questions / unresolved design choices (for meeting):
- How to combine human label signals with automated heuristics without doubling noise? Proposed: exponential backoff weighting where human labels increase confidence of an automated flag.
- Exact numeric thresholds — should be per-product baseline or single org-wide? We lean per-product but need bootstrapping defaults.
- Sampling budget: how much extra cost allowed for increased sampling during quarantine? Need finance guardrails.

Immediate next steps (short list):
- (Ava) Draft minimal telemetry schema (json props) for 6 primitives -> PR to rollout signals repo (target 2026-02-28).
- (Marcus) Wire Prometheus exporters for request_p99_ms and server_error_rate -> JIRA-ROLL-800.
- (Priya) Run 3 retrospective interviews with stewards who ran last 3 canaries (notes due 2026-03-05).
- Cross-team sync (30m): invite SRE, Safety, Evals, Console product. Proposed slots: 2026-03-02 10:00 or 2026-03-03 15:00 PT.

Draft checklist for adopting this ontology on a rollout:
- [ ] Add signal names to rollout manifest (manifest.schema.v1).
- [ ] Ensure exporters are emitting in the expected units.
- [ ] Configure Console guardrails with default thresholds.
- [ ] Setup human sampling rate for quarantine slices (default 5%).
- [ ] Document owner/operator for each rollout.

Notes to self / fragments:
- keep policy_violation alerting fast + noisy -> escalate to human only if confidence > 0.7 or repeated within window.
- consider a composite "trust_index" metric combining fidelity+policy (0..1) as a single quick visual for PMs.

Appendix: short example of a rollout manifest snippet (informal):
- model_variant: chat-redwood-1.2-q2
- signals: [fidelity.hallucination_rate, safety.policy_violation_count, reliability.request_p99_ms]
- thresholds: {fidelity.hallucination_rate: {delta_pct: 50, absolute_pct: 1.0}, safety.policy_violation_count: {absolute_pct: 0.5}}

Feedback welcome — add comments inline in this doc or ping me on Slack @ava.n.
